glosses: to crown, to wreath (to place a wreath on one's head)
to crown (to form the topmost or finishing part of)
to be situated on one's head
to crown, to end (a work, action, or series of events) well

examples.text: ...istotnie, [Rousseau] ustępem o religii zamyka i wieńczy swe dzieło.
examples.translation: ...significantly, [Rousseau] closes and crowns his text with a passage about religion.
examples.english: ...significantly, [Rousseau] closes and crowns his text with a passage about religion.

examples.text: Romantyczny nastrój dominuje w środkowej romancy, więc finałowa wirtuozeria cygańska ma efektownie wieńczyć całość.
examples.translation: A romantic style dominates in the central lyrical section [of the music], so the Gypsy-style virtuosity at the end is supposed to impressively end the whole piece.
examples.english: A romantic style dominates in the central lyrical section [of the music], so the Gypsy-style virtuosity at the end is supposed to impressively end the whole piece.

examples.text: „Potrzebne jest jakieś radykalne cięcie” – pomyślała Cesia, mijając rzeźbioną w drewnie głowę lwa, wieńczącą poręcz schodów
